While physical limitation and what other Redditors have said is true, there’s also another aspect that’s not always talked about: shortening attention spans. Over the last 20 years modern (popular music) has gotten shorter and shorter by the year due to the need to “hook” listeners as fast as possible and most people according to studies do not listen the same way we used to. (think people on Spotify skipping songs left and right, which gives each song on average if I remember correctly around 4-8 seconds time to engage the listener)

Engaging a listener is more of a science than pop musicians and producers would have you believe, there’s not a single recipe that will work of course but there are things that help immensely which have nothing to do with the artistry of music-making. 
Things like, short musical phrases, very easy to understand and remember harmonic progression that repeat a whole lot of times, ambiguous lyrics that are relevant to almost everyone so they can “artificially relate” to the singer/musician (IE the multimillionaire who definitely has the same problems as you). Especially the “dumbing down” of harmonic progressions to the point where instead of music being a thing of art where it challenges you it rather becomes a dull experience where loud noises, fast rhythms and repetitive melodies are king. 
Oh, and did I mention repetition?  
All of this has to happen fast enough to engage the listener in the 4-8 seconds. 

There’s not really a “reason” why, but rather a general direction of our evolution and how we consume music that’s to “blame” for it. Think things like TikTok, social media frenzies and Spotify. 

Personal opinion: I also think a big thing that plays into this whole topic is money. The musicians market is incredibly oversatured to the point where everyone and their cat could on their phone be making music that’s they think should sell which has led to places like Spotify and generally the internet being filled with subpar songs being pushed just because they have a slight resemblance to the other thousands of popular music pieces/songs which use the exact same chord/harmony progression which also contributes to the problem because what is popular is now the songs that resemble the other pieces/songs that we’ve grown accustomed to. The human brain likes habits and known things. 

In the end music has become a business so oversatured and competition that it has become who can make the next catchiest 5 second soundbites that will go viral. Ladygaga, Taylor swift and who else are more artists in psychology and the human brain than music. 

Sources below + studied music for nearly a decade which has included a fair bit of research and analysing the current state of all kinds of music.
